reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E9 shows laser ablation can produce CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles but does not confirm uniform elemental distribution. No cited passage demonstrates that annealing induces surface segregation in these nanoparticles, that segregation reduces cohesive energies, or that this alters melting behavior. The evidence is largely about synthesis methods, magnetic properties, or mechanical behavior, not premelting or melting mechanisms.
premises: Ultrafast laser ablation can produce equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles with uniform elemental distribution
Moderate annealing below bulk melting temperature induces selective surface segregation of lower-cohesion elements
Surface segregation locally reduces atomic cohesive energies
Reduced surface cohesive energy triggers earlier premelting onset and lowers overall melting temperature
